slides.headline: SF banana matcha: 3 ways to order it
slides.body: Banana oat milk, iced banana matcha, or a banana-and-kinako cloud? Three café menus to compare.

slides.headline: SŌHN · Dogpatch
slides.body: The menu lists Banana Oat Milk Latte with matcha: $7. Iced only. 2535 3rd St.

slides.headline: YakiniQ · Japantown
slides.body: Iced Banana Matcha Latte: $8.50 for 16 oz. 1640 Post St. Plant-milk swaps are not shown for this drink.

slides.headline: Kumo · Sunday pop-up
slides.body: Banana purée + soy cloud + kinako. Menu season: Sept 5–Jan 3. Sundays 9am–1pm, 1377 Fell St. Price not published.

slides.headline: Soy cloud ≠ dairy-free
slides.body: Kumo marks the banana drink as containing dairy. SŌHN names oat milk; ask about the full recipe. Save the guide before your next matcha run.

assets.text:
Banana matcha has options 🍌

SŌHN’s menu: banana oat milk with matcha, $7.
YakiniQ’s menu: a 16 oz iced banana matcha, $8.50.
Kumo’s seasonal menu: banana purée, soy cloud and kinako at its Sunday SF pop-up.

One detail that matters: Kumo marks its drink as containing dairy. A soy topping does not make the latte dairy-free. YakiniQ’s banana listing does not show a plant-milk swap.

These are menu finds, not tasting rankings. Which style would you try? Save the guide for addresses, hours and café sources.

slides.headline: Matcha clouds: choose your topping
slides.body: Four SF menu finds for matcha foam, cream and clouds.

slides.headline: Q · 3490 California St
slides.body: Velvet Matcha Cloud: $8.25. Q lists matcha cloud over a matcha latte. Foam ingredients are not specified.

slides.headline: Tadaima · Mission
slides.body: Salted Cheese Cream Matcha: $7.50 iced. Strawberry and pistachio cream are also listed. A plant-milk base does not confirm a dairy-free topping.

slides.headline: SŌHN or Kumo?
slides.body: SŌHN lists its iced matcha Signature Cream Top at $7. Kumo lists an in-season London Fog Matcha Latte with vanilla cloud and Earl Grey syrup.

slides.headline: Check the foam, not just the milk
slides.body: Kumo explicitly marks London Fog Matcha as containing dairy. Ask Q, Tadaima and SŌHN about topping ingredients. Menus checked Oct 7; prices before extras.

assets.text:
The topping deserves its own order decision ☁️

Q: Velvet Matcha Cloud, $8.25.
Tadaima Mission: Salted Cheese Cream Matcha, $7.50 iced.
SŌHN: matcha Signature Cream Top, $7 iced.
Kumo: seasonal London Fog Matcha with Earl Grey syrup and vanilla cloud.

These names describe different café builds. They are not interchangeable recipes, and choosing oat milk underneath does not make the foam dairy-free. Kumo explicitly lists dairy; the other menus do not confirm dairy-free cream toppings.

Save the menu guide for the drink details and sources. No tasting winner declared.

Guide: https://sanfranciscomatcha.com/guides/matcha-cold-foam-san-francisco/

SF matcha clouds: Q’s Velvet Cloud, Tadaima’s salted cheese cream, SŌHN’s cream top and Kumo’s London Fog. Check the topping ingredients: oat underneath doesn’t make cream dairy-free. Menu guide: https://sanfranciscomatcha.com/guides/matcha-cold-foam-san-francisco/

assets.voiceover: If you are chasing matcha cold foam, compare the topping. Q lists a Velvet Matcha Cloud at eight twenty-five. Tadaima has salted cheese cream for seven fifty. SŌHN lists its matcha cream top at seven dollars. Kumo’s seasonal London Fog adds Earl Grey syrup and vanilla cloud. And yes, Kumo says it contains dairy. An oat-milk base is only half the question. These are menu options, not a best-foam award.

slides.headline: Looking for soy matcha in SF?
slides.body: Three café menus that actually list soy. Start with a plain latte and check the whole recipe.

slides.headline: Il Parco · Presidio
slides.body: 12 oz matcha with soy: $6 hot or $6.30 iced. Official menu lists a $0.50 plant-milk charge. 215 Lincoln Blvd.

slides.headline: Lulu Fresh · Waterfront
slides.body: The $7 matcha product page has a soy selection, hot or iced. Check modifier totals at checkout. 50 Francisco St, Suite 105.

slides.headline: YakiniQ · Japantown
slides.body: 12 oz Matcha Latte: $7 + $0.75 soy; iced adds $0.25. The modifier says Extra Soy Milk—ask for replacement, not addition.

slides.headline: Milk swap is step one
slides.body: Ask about cream toppings and premixed bases too. Lactose-free dairy is still dairy. Save the guide for menu links and current hours.

assets.text:
Soy matcha seekers: here are three menus to save 🌱

Il Parco lists soy as a milk alternative: a 12 oz matcha is $6 hot or $6.30 iced with the surcharge.
Lulu Fresh’s $7 matcha product page has a soy selection; check checkout for modifiers.
YakiniQ lists soy on its matcha ordering page for $0.75.

At YakiniQ, the option is called Extra Soy Milk. Specify that you want soy to replace the dairy milk. And at every café, check cream or premixed ingredients if you avoid dairy.

Soy is verified from menus here—not an allergy certification. Full addresses, hours and sources in the guide.

Guide: https://sanfranciscomatcha.com/guides/soy-milk-matcha-san-francisco/

Soy matcha in SF: Il Parco, Lulu Fresh and YakiniQ list it. At YakiniQ the modifier says “Extra Soy Milk”—ask for replacement. Check toppings too; lactose-free dairy is still dairy. Sources: https://sanfranciscomatcha.com/guides/soy-milk-matcha-san-francisco/

assets.voiceover: If you prefer soy with matcha, three San Francisco menus explicitly list it. Il Parco’s twelve-ounce matcha with soy is six dollars hot or six thirty iced. Lulu Fresh lets you select soy on its matcha page. YakiniQ lists soy for seventy-five cents extra. Its modifier says extra soy milk, so make clear that you want a replacement. Check the topping and base too. Lactose-free dairy is still dairy. The guide links every menu.

slides.headline: Strawberry matcha: latte or topping?
slides.body: Four SF menus, two useful questions: where does the strawberry go, and what is in the cream?

slides.headline: Stonemill · Valencia
slides.body: Cold Strawberry Latte has a matcha or hojicha choice, milk and cane sugar. Oat substitution is listed. Choose matcha.

slides.headline: Four Chairs · Mission St
slides.body: Strawberry Matcha: $7. Oatly or almond adds $1. Menu address: 3282 Mission St.

slides.headline: Cloud or cream?
slides.body: Q lists Matcha Strawberry Cloud at $8.25. Tadaima Mission lists Matcha Latte with Strawberry Cream at $7.75 iced, before substitutions.

slides.headline: Ask before swapping milk
slides.body: Q’s cloud ingredients are not specified. Tadaima does not list its cream as dairy-free. Plant milk underneath does not settle that question. Save the guide for sources.

assets.text:
Strawberry in the latte or strawberry on top? 🍓

Stonemill lists a Cold Strawberry Latte with your choice of matcha or hojicha.
Four Chairs lists Strawberry Matcha at $7, with $1 Oatly or almond substitutions.
Q lists Matcha Strawberry Cloud at $8.25.
Tadaima Mission lists Strawberry Cream Matcha at $7.75 iced before milk swaps.

We checked the menus, not a side-by-side tasting. Sweetness and topping recipes vary. Ask about the cream separately if you need a dairy-free order.

Save this before your next café stop; the guide has menu links, addresses and prices.

Strawberry matcha in SF: Stonemill’s fruit latte, Four Chairs’ $7 order, Q’s strawberry cloud or Tadaima’s strawberry cream. Plant milk doesn’t confirm a dairy-free topping. Compare the menus: https://sanfranciscomatcha.com/guides/strawberry-matcha-san-francisco/

assets.voiceover: Strawberry matcha is not one recipe. Stonemill lists a strawberry latte with a matcha or hojicha choice. Four Chairs lists Strawberry Matcha at seven dollars. Q puts strawberry in its cloud topping. Tadaima has strawberry cream over an iced matcha latte. So ask where the fruit goes—and what is in the topping. Oat underneath does not confirm dairy-free cream. Our guide compares the menus without pretending these are tasting rankings.

slides.headline: Want the tea to be the focus?
slides.body: Three SF cafés documenting their matcha sourcing or hand-whisking.

slides.headline: Stonemill · 561 Valencia St
slides.body: The menu names Hand Whisked Matcha made with First Crop matcha. It also lists a water-based Matchacano.

slides.headline: Nagomi · 74 New Montgomery St
slides.body: The café describes hand-whisking Oyaizu Seicha’s Heavenly Sky matcha from Shizuoka. Its site names Straus dairy milk for lattes.

slides.headline: Pixlcat · 519 Clement St
slides.body: The café describes hot or iced organic matcha lattes using ceremonial-grade Kyoto Uji matcha. Milk choices are not specified on that page.

slides.headline: Sourcing is a starting point
slides.body: Ceremonial is the café’s description, not our quality award. Ask for a simple tea or plain latte if you want to compare. Sources and visit notes in the guide.

Nagomi describes hand-whisking matcha from Shizuoka producer Oyaizu Seicha.
Pixlcat describes ceremonial-grade Kyoto Uji matcha in its organic lattes.

These are café sourcing and preparation claims, linked in our guide. “Ceremonial” alone is not our quality award, and we haven’t invented tasting scores.

slides.headline: SF matcha under $7
slides.body: Four official menus with qualifying base orders. Before tax, tip and extras.

slides.headline: Paper Son · Downtown
slides.body: Matcha Latte or Matcha Passionfruit Soda: $6. Oat or almond adds $0.25 to the latte. 303 2nd St N102.

slides.headline: Il Parco · Presidio
slides.body: 12 oz matcha: $5.50 hot or $5.80 iced. Soy, oat or almond adds $0.50, keeping that size below $7 before tax.

slides.headline: Tadaima or SŌHN?
slides.body: Tadaima Mission: $6.25 hot / $6.75 iced, before swaps. SŌHN: Matcha Latte or Matchacano, $6; oat and almond alternatives listed free.

slides.headline: Watch the modifiers
slides.body: Tadaima’s $0.75 milk swap brings hot to $7 and iced to $7.50. No café discount is implied. Check the checkout total; save the price guide.
